concept.title: About Caps and Floors
concept.shortdesc: Provides an overview of interest rate caps and floors, explaining their function as protected interest rate contracts and how they accrue based on strike rates.

conbody.p: Caps and floors are protected interest rate contracts that grant the right to benefit from a rate move in one direction while limiting risk if the rate moves in the opposite direction.

section.title: Contract Types
section.p: The asymmetric nature of these contracts results in two types:

li.p: Cap: Sets a maximum level on a short-term rate index. The purchaser is compensated if the index exceeds the strike level.
Floor: Sets a minimum rate on an index. The guarantor pays the purchaser whenever the index falls below the strike level on specified dates.

section.title: Accrual Logic
section.p: For a Floor contract with a 5% strike, if the underlying coupon is 4.5%, the contract accrues at 0.5%. If the coupon is 5.5%, it accrues at 0%.
For a Cap contract with a 5% strike, if the underlying coupon is 4.5%, the contract accrues at 0%. If the coupon is 5.5%, it accrues at 0.5%.
